# A relational source-withdrawal witness with an exact all-one profile

Author: proteinfolding-gpt. Date: 2026-10-18 America/Phoenix.
Source baseline: `5a0827cf6f130a858465c03e279f268efdf772e1`.
Status: **AUTHOR ANALYTICAL CONSTRUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING**.
No scientific program was run. No physical interaction or receiver access is claimed derived.

## Constructive advance

The existing common-predecessor witness makes the source distinction invariant under palette relabelling, but its reference branch makes the root hitting number rise to two in one completed branch. Here a fixed binary carrier places that same reference below an unchanged full-support parent. Both preparations and an explicit completion then preserve h=1 at every internal vertex.

This joins three useful properties in one native-support witness: a common preparation seed with an unchanged receiver record; a relational distinction that survives relabelling; and a lawful source-withdrawal completion with zero hitting-profile excursion. Every lawful immediate endpoint of the specified source withdrawal still forces the receiver answer, independently of the chosen completion path.

This is mathematical support for the existing source-withdrawal native-mechanism candidate. It does not replace the remaining source-event binding or owned-record interface with another supplied quantum encoding.

## 1. Fixed native carrier

Use the inherited nonempty nested-support category. The palette is P={a,b0,b1}. The fixed binary tree has edges

    (o,u), (o,t), (u,v), (u,w), (t,z), (t,k).                 (1)

The source is u; v,w are receiver leaves; z,k carry a common reference. The root support is P. Every other support is a nonempty subset of its parent's support. A primitive adds or deletes one label incidence at one nonroot vertex, preserving these constraints.

All seven vertices belong to the initial carrier. No vertex, palette label or new edit type is introduced during the history. This uses the inherited binary-support category; it does not change any frozen four-child campaign or borrow its bounded certification.

At each internal x, h_x is the smallest size of a label set meeting every immediate child support. Write q_o=q_u=q_t=1 and D_q=sum_x |h_x-q_x|.

## 2. Common preparation with a blank receiver

Begin at the common seed

    S_o=P; S_u=S_t=S_v=S_w=S_z=S_k={a}.                     (2)

Apply the same six edits in both preparations:

    +b0(t), +b1(t), +b0(z), +b0(k), +b0(u), +b1(u).         (3)

The resulting common predecessor H has

    S_u=S_t=P; S_v=S_w={a}; S_z=S_k={a,b0}.                 (4)

Then make one branch edit:

    H -- -b1(u) --> F0,
    H -- -b0(u) --> F1.                                    (5)

Thus in F_s,

    S_u={a,b_s}; S_t=P; S_v=S_w={a}; S_z=S_k={a,b0}.        (6)

Every edit is legal. Additions at u,t are allowed by the root P. The reference additions are allowed after t contains b0. The branch deletion at u removes a label absent from both its children, and leaves a at u.

Every child support contains a throughout preparation, so h_o=h_u=h_t=1 at every intermediate state. Consequently D_q=0, with no external band filter.

The mathematical receiver record proposed for this construction is (S_v,S_w,S_z,S_k), with common fixed references. Its entire preparation history is identical across the two branches. Source u is excluded. This record includes a reference branch as well as the receiving leaves; it is explicitly not a derivation of single-vertex access or an assumption that every vertex sees all these rows.

The seed and the actual execution of the preparation remain declared/conditional. Seven legal edits from a common seed establish relative reachability, not physical generation or a positive preparation probability.

## 3. The source distinction is relational

At F_s, t is the only nonroot vertex with support cardinality three. Any rooted-tree isomorphism combined with a global palette permutation must therefore preserve t and its sibling u. It may exchange z and k, whose supports are identical, and v and w, likewise identical.

The invariant

    I_s=|S_u intersection S_z|                              (7)

has I_0=2 and I_1=1. Therefore F0 and F1 cannot be identified by any simultaneous palette permutation and rooted-tree automorphism. This is stronger than relying on externally fixed b-label names. It remains true if the category already fixes vertex order.

The receiver is not given I_s initially: it depends on the excluded source row S_u. The common reference itself contains no branch-specific input.

## 4. Same source event, complete native path

The specified event in both branches is -a(u), with source input {a,b_s}. A completion is

    +b_s(v), +b_s(w), -a(v), -a(w), -a(u).                 (8)

Its supports are as follows; t,z,k remain as in (6).

| State | S_u | S_v | S_w |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F_s | {a,b_s} | {a} | {a} |
| After +b_s(v) | {a,b_s} | {a,b_s} | {a} |
| After +b_s(w) | {a,b_s} | {a,b_s} | {a,b_s} |
| After -a(v) | {a,b_s} | {b_s} | {a,b_s} |
| After -a(w) | {a,b_s} | {b_s} | {b_s} |
| After -a(u) | {b_s} | {b_s} | {b_s} |

Each addition is allowed by u; each receiver deletion leaves b_s; the final source deletion is legal once a is absent from both children.

At u, the child supports share a throughout the additions and share b_s throughout the deletions. Hence h_u=1. At t the identical nonempty child supports remain {a,b0}, so h_t=1. At o, the fixed child support S_t=P intersects every nonempty S_u, so h_o=1 throughout. Therefore

    D_q=0 along preparation (3)-(5) and completion (8).     (9)

There are twelve edits in this displayed history for either branch. This is a path length, not an enumeration count or a measured physical duration.

The all-one claim concerns this explicit completion and any other completion independently satisfying that profile. It does NOT claim that every lawful completion preserves h=1 at intermediate states. For example, removing a at v before adding b_s at w leaves child supports {b_s} and {a}, temporarily giving h_u=2. Such a history is legal in the bare category.

## 5. Endpoint forcing does not depend on the displayed path

Consider any native history on this fixed carrier ending immediately after the specified source deletion, with source input {a,b_s} at that event and the reference branch fixed. Immediately afterward S_u={b_s}. Nonemptiness and nesting give

    empty != S_v subset {b_s}, empty != S_w subset {b_s},
    hence S_v=S_w={b_s}.                                  (10)

This is the existing source-withdrawal argument applied to the enlarged fixed carrier. No unique path, source-blind selection rule, or separate receiver-success premise is needed for this endpoint implication. The displayed path proves that the profile-preserving completion class is nonempty.

An invariant endpoint discriminator using the receiver/reference record is

    Q=1[S_v intersection S_z is nonempty].
    Q_0=1; Q_1=0.                                         (11)

Initially Q=1 in both branches. At completion the full receiver/reference records differ and (11) separates them. Q alone is not an event receipt: its initial value coincides with one completed branch. If an incomplete history must be distinguished, the unchanged common blank label/reference and the full declared record need their own specified decoder, as in the prior construction.

For any probability distributions supported on lawful completed histories with these fixed source-event inputs and references, the mathematical endpoint record laws separate perfectly. This statement supplies no distribution, completion probability, sampling protocol or actual access.

The final deletion is not the first action in (8). Indeed, it cannot be legal while either receiver still contains a. Thus (10) is a joint-completion consequence: source commitment entails that the receiver adjustment has already happened. It is not an assertion that the final deletion subsequently writes the record, nor a backward-time influence. Time remains pruning / ordered update.

## 6. Why the reference placement works

The earlier reference sat directly beside the source at the root. The source endpoint {b1} and reference {a,b0} were then disjoint, forcing a two-label root cover.

Here the root compares {b_s} with P, so one label always covers its children. The informative reference {a,b0} remains below t and is unchanged. Its relation to the receiver leaf still distinguishes the branches. No new constraint or physical coupling is added: only the initial fixed native tree differs.

The reference does not secretly select the completion. Equation (10) uses only the source singleton and native nesting/nonemptiness; it does not use S_z, S_k or their intersection test. The reference makes the distinction relational and readable under the stated mathematical interface. It does not cause the forced endpoint.

## 7. Earned result and remaining construction

Earned analytically here: one fully binary fixed-carrier witness simultaneously has common-seed reachability, branch-blind receiver preparation history, palette-invariant source distinction, a twelve-edit zero-excursion history, and the inherited all-completion endpoint implication. This removes the earlier witness's profile excursion without trading away its relational distinction.

Still open: actual realization of the common seed/preparation; identification of an existing actual event with the specified support withdrawal; and ownership/access to the receiver and reference rows. Merely transposing indexed views into support rows does not earn access. No event probability, invocation policy, measurement gate, new register or grade-to-state dictionary is supplied.

The next constructive task is to identify those rows with an already owned native retained record. The candidate no longer needs a new quantum-state assignment merely to express its result, and a fixed-profile restriction does not block this explicit path. Neither fact establishes that the rows are physically available.

## 8. Exact dependencies and review target

All following paths are in ResearchHistory/UQCF-GEM at the immutable baseline above:

- demos/v16.53-four-child-boundary/NATIVE_ADMISSIBILITY.md: nonempty nesting, fixed root and one-incidence edit definition; the general grammar is used, not a new claim about its four-child certification.
- research/physical-bridge/receiver_move_interface/RESULT.md, sections 1-2: exact native addition/deletion conditions.
- research/physical-bridge/source_withdrawal_completion/WORKING_CONSTRUCTION.md: forced singleton endpoint, legal completion and enactment/access distinctions.
- research/physical-bridge/source_withdrawal_completion/PREPARABILITY_COMMON_PREDECESSOR.md: common seed, relational reference and the disclosed profile excursion being removed.
- research/physical-bridge/STANDING_DIRECTIVE.md: constructive priority and independent Gemini review requirement.

Independent review should reconstruct every displayed edit, check all three internal hitting numbers at every phase, challenge the relabelling argument and the initial receiver interface, distinguish existence of a zero-excursion path from a claim about all paths, and preserve the temporal/enactment/access qualifications. It must receive this full text and the exact dependencies, not only this result summary.

This is a new working proof, not a numerical preregistration or accepted review. All findings above were developed before any execution. Existing frozen records remain unchanged. No native milestone, main merge or numbered-stage closure is claimed.

Placing the common reference under its own unchanged full-support parent removes the earlier reference witness's root-profile excursion.

The displayed path has seven preparation edits and five completion edits. These are analytical path lengths, not numerical enumeration counts. The all-completion receiver endpoint follows from nonempty nested supports when the specified source withdrawal commits. # v15.11 — Ontology Continuity / Retained-Algebra and Actual-Record Reconciliation

**Status:** locally verified reconciliation; repository integration remains separate.  
**Result:** `CONTINUITY_RESTORED_CONDITIONAL_ORDINAL_ORDER_PRESERVED`  
**New physical axioms adopted:** none. **Scientific breakthrough:** false. **Pillar 3:** OPEN.

## 1. Correction, not a restart

The older Library archive contains reversible pre-time motion (v10.8), a frozen non-repair boundary (v10.21), conditional nonselective pruning (v11.1), conditional realized-record history (v11.2), and conditional ordinal event time (v11.3). v11.4 already establishes duration nonuniqueness; v11.5 proposes a separate conditional clock bridge.

Those reports were absent from the v15.10 dependency manifest. Its fixed-known-potential exponential-reweighting lemma remains valid, but its results do not establish archive-wide absence of a noninjective operation or conditional ordinal-time construction. The original v15.10 code, report, summary, and measured values are preserved. `../v15.10/CONTINUITY_NOTICE.md` withdraws the overbroad interpretation without rewriting the historical snapshot.

This reconciliation reconstructs small examples independently. It is not a rerun of every original executable or a formal proof-check of the entire archive.

## 2. The ontology boundary

Pre-time motion is a reversible relational transformation, not motion along an imported clock:

\[
x\mapsto g x,\qquad g^{-1}g x=x.
\]

Composition of transformations need not be an order of irreversible events. A software loop is necessary to execute many calculations; its existence neither derives physical time nor invalidates a pre-time calculation. The full coupled V1153 system has not been proved reversible merely by inverting its isolated fixed-potential weight tilt.

The user's proposed onset of entropy and time at irreversible observational choice is retained as an ontological interpretation and research target. It is not used as an observable, a branch-selection algorithm, or evidence for a mathematical theorem. No theological label, elapsed-time parameter, entropy objective, or downstream gravity score selects the operations below.

## 3. Restore the earned conditional chain

**RAS:** a retained observable algebra is supplied. In finite-dimensional tracial theory the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto it is then canonical. RAS is an existing explicit primitive, not a conclusion of symmetry alone.

For the supplied qubit algebra spanned by I and Z,

\[
E_Z(\rho)=\tfrac12(\rho+Z\rho Z),\qquad
E_Z(|+\rangle\langle+|)=E_Z(|-\rangle\langle-|)=I/2.
\]

Input trace distance is 1 and output distance is 0. The channel loses recoverable distinctions even though each density matrix's rank increases from 1 to 2. Thus **density-matrix support reduction is not required for information loss**. The relevant property is distinguishability in the declared retained description. An unchanged fixed state or repeated application of the same idempotent projection does not certify another strict loss event.

**RCR:** an actual positive-weight central record is supplied. The code raises an error if no record is supplied; it contains no hidden sampling, maximum-weight choice, or preferred outcome. The same dephasing channel admits both projective and random-unitary instrument descriptions. Therefore the channel alone does not settle actuality or event semantics.

**Record-compatible refinement:** given RAS and RCR along a strict compatible chain, projection inclusion defines

\[
e\preceq f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad z_f\le z_e.
\]

On distinct nested projections this is antisymmetric and transitive. Strict inclusion reduces finite rank, so the strict relation has no cycle. Each realized finite chain has an ordinal position without a clock. Independent chains retain only their partial order; the two length-two chains in the control admit six total interleavings. This restores v11.3's **conditional ordinal-time result**, not an unconditional physical-time derivation.

## 4. Make record compatibility explicit

Nested algebras alone are insufficient. Let

\[
\mathcal A=M_2\oplus M_2,\qquad
\mathcal B=\{\operatorname{diag}(T,T):T\in M_2\}\subset\mathcal A.
\]

Their conditional expectations obey the nesting identity, but the old central record \(Q_A=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,0)\) is sent to \(I_4/2\). The old center has dimension 2 and the new center dimension 1. So a legal algebra reduction can erase the earlier classical distinction rather than refine it.

A sufficient record-preservation condition is

\[
Z(\mathcal A)\subseteq\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
Z(\mathcal A)\subseteq Z(\mathcal B).
\]

Proof: an old central element retained in B still commutes with every element of B because it commuted with all of A. Its projection therefore decomposes into new central sectors. This spells out the older report's **record-compatible** premise; it is not silently adopted as a new physical law selecting B.

Also, an arbitrary noninjective map need not define acyclic succession: the map `(0,1,2) -> (1,0,0)` has a two-cycle. The specific v15.10 `8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1` witness is valid, but noninjectivity by itself is not a universal time-order theorem. Strict refinement/recoverability descent is load-bearing.

## 5. State the scope of irreversibility

A coherent CNOT dilation keeps the two inputs distinguishable in the joint output (trace distance 1), while the retained marginal makes them identical (distance 0). Keeping only a classical Z-outcome flag also fails to restore their relative phase. Reversing the full coherent operation succeeds exactly in this finite control.

This does not adopt a hidden environment as the ontology or deny objective collapse. It shows what must be specified before asserting global information destruction: which coherent degrees of freedom, records, and recovery operations are actually retained. A conditional expectation proves loss relative to its retained algebra; it does not by itself prove destruction of information in every possible enlarged description.

For the same fixture, ordinary von Neumann entropy is `log(2)` after nonselective dephasing and zero in a selected pure branch. The neutral reference I/2 also has that mathematical entropy. These are diagnostics, not a derivation of physical entropy production. No entropy-based collapse selector or equation equating entropy with elapsed time is introduced.

## 6. Do not restart the clock search

v11.4 already provides the inequivalent family

\[
D_p(\mathcal A\to\mathcal B)=\log\frac{\sum_i a_i^p}{\sum_j b_j^p},\qquad p>1.
\]

Our reconstructed block chain `[4] -> [2,2] -> [2,1,1] -> [1,1,1,1]` yields different p=2 and p=3 interval ratios even after the first interval is normalized to 1. The separation is about 0.10748. v11.5's Motion-Capacity Clock Calibration is a separate physical premise, not an automatic consequence of motion or record order. It is recorded, not adopted or rederived here.

## 7. Evidence and reproducibility

Twenty regression tests were written first. The recorded local RED run failed all twenty with the intended absent-implementation assertion. The subsequent GREEN run passed all twenty. Local execution used Python 3.13.5 and NumPy 2.3.5. Remote CI, when run, is a separate pinned-environment verification, not retroactive evidence of remote RED.

`SUMMARY.json` freezes measured diagnostics; scientific checks independently use absolute tolerances of 1e-12 for numerical identities and explicit finite separation checks. Archive float comparison uses `rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-12`; integer, boolean, and categorical fields are exact.

`SOURCE_MANIFEST.json` records SHA-256 hashes for seven original Library snapshots and verbatim excerpt ranges. All seven originals and exact excerpt ranges were checked locally. **Repository CI without `--sources` checks the committed excerpts only; it does not reread unavailable Library originals.** The downloadable bundle includes all original source bytes for full verification. Digests demonstrate version identity, not mathematical truth.

Run from this gate directory:

```sh
python -m unittest -v test_continuity.py
python ontology_continuity_audit.py --check
# With the bundled original reports:
python ontology_continuity_audit.py --check --sources ../source_archive
```

Use the actual source directory path when running from a different layout. The bundle README gives its exact command.

## 8. Current blocker and stop boundary

The correct status is no longer “no pruning operation or ordinal history exists.” It is:

- reversible pre-time motion: preserved;
- irreversible reduction relative to a supplied retained algebra: conditional construction preserved;
- actual record and compatible ordinal history: preserved conditional on RAS, RCR, and strict record refinement;
- those primitives as an unconditional physical collapse/actuality law: not established here;
- physical entropy production and duration: not supplied by naming the operation pruning;
- source-semantics and carrier results: unchanged within their audited premises.

Do not select RAS or RCR by downstream gravity, do not rename a loop as time, and do not turn a diagnostic entropy into the physical second law. The next unresolved issue must be located against the full older dependency ledger before any new primitive or versioned rediscovery is proposed.

# Draft 14 review: one existing imperfect record can suffice

Author: proteinfolding-gpt. Date: 2026-10-18 (America/Phoenix).
Inspected parent: `ebc87a4910f1210d4645eec849fb3245827d9ea0`.
Status: analytical follow-up, not independent Gemini acceptance. Native receiver access **NOT_DERIVED**.

## 1. Progress and correction disposition

Draft 14 (`8c9790ed`) adopted the draft-13 availability finding from `566b9b8d`: soundness gives A_av contained in D_p; obtaining equality also requires completeness. Its section 20 usefully classifies finite sound availability algebras as partition algebras and computes their exact contrasts. Under its explicit unit-invariance premise, a nontrivial such algebra is the empty/positive algebra C*(Q_p).

The remaining stale section-19 corollary, premise summary and next-step text have been reconciled in CONSTRUCTION.md [GPT14]. The full-coordinate conclusion now includes completeness (A3), the canonical state representation and the relevant slice. Locality alone does not establish pre-event coordinate access. Occupancy access is weaker than full-coordinate access when multiple positive grades are reachable; (A3') does not restore full (H-J) in that case.

The partition proof, data-processing argument and two-orbit classification support the stated conditional conclusions. This is an author-side analytical assessment, not a new review verdict. Draft 14's exploratory counts were not rerun and are not independent evidence. Its finite-register quantum claims remain finite; the classical background statements below allow any nonnegative Borel probability law. Unit invariance means the stated all-positive-rescalings condition, not merely relabelling a fixed finite coordinate list.

## 2. A single fixed binary effect, without algebra completeness

Keep the declared single-pruning map, the canonical address representation and an initially blind one-location source pair: the source contributes grade g > 0 in the plus preparation and is absent in the minus preparation. The common post-event background fiber has law nu on [0,infinity). These assumptions give output coordinate laws nu shifted by g and nu. They do not yet prove native receiver access.

Suppose an **already available**, common binary measurement has effect E, with 0 <= E <= I, local to the receiver and event-determined in the sense of section 19. Suppose its diagonal response is unit-free. The positive half-line is a single scaling orbit, so for some a,b in [0,1],

    E = a (I-Q_p) + b Q_p,   Q_p = 1[N_p' > 0].             (1)

Here a and b are the existing effect's empty and occupied response probabilities. They are to be derived from that record's source, not chosen to create a signal. Equation (1) classifies that effect; it does not install an occupancy measurement. Nonconstancy means a != b when both sectors are reachable.

Let P = 1[N_in > 0]. Theorem 19.4(b) and linearity give, for every finite-dimensional coherent extension of the forced classical map,

    Phi*(E) = a(I-P) + bP.                                  (2)

This concerns the probability of the already available binary outcome. It needs neither a specified microscopic coherent extension nor assumption (A0) that access is closed under forming an algebra.

Write z = nu({0}). Since background grades are nonnegative and g > 0, the plus output is always positive. Thus the probabilities of that binary outcome are

    p_plus  = b,
    p_minus = a z + b(1-z),
    TV(Bern(p_plus), Bern(p_minus)) = |b-a| z.                (3)

Equation (3) follows by integration of the two-valued response and applies to arbitrary nonnegative Borel backgrounds, including mixtures with continuous parts. It does not represent a continuous law as a trace-class diagonal state on l2(R). For the one-location pair the complete pre-event receiver states agree, hence every initially available effect is blind. Consequently this particular binary record transfers a distinction exactly when

    a != b  and  nu({0}) > 0.                               (4)

This is the same occupancy criterion with a response factor |b-a|. A sharp reader has |b-a|=1; a noisy existing reader can have 0<|b-a|<1. The result allows an imperfect probability record without demanding error-free decoding of a single realized outcome.

One must not infer that Q_p itself is measurable from E being measurable. Although Q_p=(E-aI)/(b-a) as operators when a!=b, that affine expression is not generally a stochastic post-processing of a binary outcome. For example, when a=1/4 and b=3/4, any relabelling by probabilities u,v in [0,1] yields response u+(v-u)p. Achieving responses 0 at p=a and 1 at p=b would require |v-u|=2, which is impossible. Additional access operations or repeated independent preparations are not assumed here.

For the hand-calculated law nu=(delta_0+delta_2)/2 and g=1, that existing response would give p_minus=1/2, p_plus=3/4 and contrast 1/4. This is an illustration of (3), not a proposed mechanism or an empirical calibration. The controls a=b and z=0 give zero contrast directly.

## 3. The actual-record target is a response correspondence

The previously inspected frozen v15.16 record model already has sector effects Q_C and input pullbacks P_C, with

    Tr[Q_C D_T(V sigma V*)] = Tr[P_C sigma].                  (5)

Its source identities and scope are in GPT_DRAFT12_SOURCES.json and the prior correspondence note. Equation (5) preserves the probability of an existing record; it does not derive the initial record-writing event. A sector must be receiver-local and retained in the actual accessible record algebra, as specified in that note.

For a fixed inherited sector C and independently justified native states sigma_x, an adequate weaker target than a sharp grade-sector match is

    Tr[P_C sigma_x] = a + (b-a) 1[x_p+x_l > 0],   a != b.    (6)

Equation (6) would give (3) for the corresponding preparation mixtures, provided (5) describes the actual event/record and the whole receiver is initially blind. The response need only hold on the admissible native preparation family. One does not need to promote it to a full operator identity on unprepared states. A sharp P_C can have a noisy response on that family.

Equation (6) is an outstanding source-to-state/record obligation, not an established property of the frozen encoding. No basis, sigma_x, mask, controller or a,b is selected here to enforce it. For a general existing effect with a non-unit-free native response f, the exact target is simply a nonzero integral of f(y+g)-f(y) against nu; the milestone does not require unit invariance if an independently justified reference already exists.

## 4. Next scientific action and review scope

Continue from the inherited record's fixed input pullback and the native state assignment. Derive the response in (6), or another genuinely separating response, from those sources. Then establish receiver ownership/retention, complete initial blindness and preparability for the same pair. A nonzero algebra dimension, a formal changing coordinate, or a matching binary label is insufficient by itself. This follow-up reduces the requested strength of the readout; it does not discharge the remaining native assumptions.

The next exact Gemini review packet should include the revised section-18 arbitrary-Borel proofs and scope corrections, corrected section 19, section 20, this follow-up and their source correspondence. Original frozen draft-12 acceptance covers its original text only.
